request.state: A Rust compiler and its owning exact-value implementation live in one repository. Static Money defaults currently fail explicitly. The private native Values library already exports validated decimal parsing, checked Money construction from major-unit integer or decimal amounts, and scalar Money wire encoding. It owns currency tables, half-even rounding and int64 overflow. Native bindings already depend on that library by Cargo path; there is no cycle or separately published crate. Needed transitive crates are locally cached. Build catalogs carry signatures rather than an evaluator. We need real constant model-field and operation-parameter defaults without reimplementing arithmetic, currency facts or codecs. Compare alternatives by the same standards: semantic parity with the public JavaScript owner, clear maintenance ownership, small complete implementation, and a self-contained single-binary compiler. Constant scalar inputs are supported; general expression evaluation is excluded. Which reuse boundary should be selected? Advice does not itself approve the change.

money_default_boundary.instructions: Choose using equal stated outcomes; weigh coupling against added API or host requirements and retain uncertainty.

criteria.direct_owner: Reuse current exported Rust owner functions via a local Cargo dependency and adapt only literal inputs/output structure in compiler. Minimal additional code and no JavaScript host; the compiler explicitly depends on private module/carrier stability and takes the owner dependencies.
criteria.owner_facade: First expose a focused Money-default evaluator from the Rust owner, then consume it through Cargo. Constructor/codec semantics stay shared and private carriers are hidden; adds an API and coordinated owner work without removing native dependencies.
criteria.public_js_process: Evaluate defaults using an external JavaScript runtime and installed public Values package. Keeps the public package as the direct API; adds process orchestration and required host installation instead of a Rust owner dependency, affecting standalone compilation.
